request: Systematically check the previously unmarked scientific-name explanations against sources and correct all three languages as necessary.
method: Read the meaning clauses for all 1,191 target terms against their cited dictionary entries or research publications; review fuller passages and taxonomic context where wording, competing analyses, identities or motives required it.

Review the complete English explanations and the German/Dutch meanings; compare the explicit word-component definitions across all three languages. Check extraction artefacts and source-word forms separately.

Use typographic dictionary entries, follow lowercase epithet and genus cross-references, and explicitly record eight catalogue/source spelling variants. A header match alone is not the semantic review.

Distinguish word meaning, word formation, old bird identifications, later name transfers, personal identity and documented dedication. An inferred naming motive is qualified rather than stated as an author’s documented intent.

Record every starting term, including retained terms, using hashes of the before/after runtime records. Source passage hashes identify the temporary extraction used for dictionary checks; no book text is distributed in this report.
limits: This is a systematic editorial source check, not an independent historical reconstruction from every original naming publication. Most explanations rely on Jobling’s 2010 dictionary; quoted alternative analyses are attributed to it where their originals were not independently consulted.
Wember (2005) was not available in full text and was not used as an individually consulted source.

The DHLE aura page could not be retrieved in this pass. Its Indigenous-origin finding is carried forward from the documented 8 November full-text review; the current RAE DLE cross-check confirms only the broader American-origin vulture word.

Mearns, Gouraud & Chevrier (2015) was checked through the authors’ published abstract, which explicitly supplies the Richard identity, dates and postal role used in the explanation; the full article was not accessible.

Existing BnF person-identity evidence for Audouin is retained from the earlier review. This pass newly checks Payraudeau’s explicit dedication on p. 464 and corrects the primary/identity source scopes.
Uncertainty markers identify material uncertainty in the explanation. Their absence does not certify an exact modern identification for every ancient bird word or establish a remote prehistoric root.
